title: A city-scale map board with location pins — V1's muster board, ported and re-grimed
summary: V1's console.js had a working map board — a background image with placed, collision-avoiding location pins (.bi-marker), each opening a card with a photo, a fix line (bearing/range) and a risk gauge. The pure placement math and the CSS both still exist and are untouched; nothing in the live Foundry module renders them yet. This is where and how they would.
description:
Prompted directly by Ingram (2026-09-17, the same pass that rebuilt the command bar into 'the deck'): 'Think about how the city map UI would look, V1 of the UI had character frames and map pin visuals which you need to create too.'

Character frames turned out to already be built and live-verified (design/theatre-of-the-mind-staging.md, built 2026-09-07, confirmed still working against the new deck in the same session this idea was captured) — that half of the ask was already done, just in a part of the codebase the deck work hadn't touched. Map pins are the genuine gap: `core/marker-layout.mjs` (placeMarker/layoutMarkers — anchor+card+stem placement with collision avoidance, exclusion rects, a priority order) is fully built and unit-tested, and `.bi-marker`/`.bi-marker__card`/`.bi-marker__scope`/`.bi-marker__risk`/`.bi-marker__muster` is fully built in bi-components.css (re-grimed to match the deck's new dust/wear pass in the same session) — but BOTH are imported and used only by `design/ui/console.js`, the standalone V1 prototype. Zero live template in `module/blank-inheritance/templates/` references either. This entry exists so that gap doesn't get rediscovered from scratch, and so nobody re-derives the placement math or re-invents the pin CSS before checking here first.

**What V1's board actually was, concretely** (`design/ui/console.js`'s `MARKERS` array and `renderMarkers()`): a background scene image with several placed dots (`{id, x, y (fractions of the scene box), kind, code, name, status, risk, detail, jp, note, crew}`), each dot growing a stem to a nearby floating card — the SAME `.bi-marker__card` vocabulary theatre-of-the-mind-staging.md borrowed for character frames, but with the two pieces that document explicitly said NOT to carry over to a person: the risk gauge (`.bi-marker__risk`, a 5-step amber/vermilion band) and the muster berths (`.bi-marker__muster`, who has signed on to an operation at that location). Those two are exactly what belongs to a PLACE rather than a PERSON, and they are the reason `.bi-marker` in its full form is still worth keeping distinct from `.bi-frame`.

**Why nothing has been built yet, honestly:** there is no real location data to point pins at. `data/campaign/` has no locations file, no coordinates, no map image assigned to any scene the way `data/campaign/stage-demo.json` assigns portraits and backgrounds for the character-frame demo. Building the Foundry-facing renderer without real data would mean either inventing place names (against this project's standing discipline — CLAUDE.md, and the same reasoning that kept `stage-demo.json` explicitly labelled DEMO, not canon) or shipping an empty shell nobody can evaluate. `day-ring.mjs`'s own header already names the intended home for this: 'downtime scheduling is part of theatre of the mind... just done from an overview map of the whole city' — so the natural anchor is the downtime/segment zone, at city scale, once there are real place names and a real map image to hang pins on.

**The concrete technical plan, once that data exists** (nothing here is a commitment, just the shape the work would take, so it doesn't have to be re-derived): a `city.schema.json`-shaped location list (name, coordinates as fractions of a map image, a status/risk reading, an optional standing offer or scene hook) feeding `layoutMarkers()` unchanged; a background Scene the same way theatre-of-the-mind staging already uses a real Foundry Scene rather than a second rendering surface (design/theatre-of-the-mind-staging.md §6's structural call applies here too — don't rebuild what Foundry Scenes already do); a thin `foundry/city-board.mjs` adapter mirroring `foundry/cast.mjs`'s shape (read live data, hand plain objects to the pure layout function); and `.bi-marker__risk`/`__muster` reactivated for exactly the sign-up-mechanics use they were held back from on a person's frame.

**What's already provably fine and needs no further design work:** the placement engine itself. `core/marker-layout.mjs`'s collision avoidance, exclusion rects and priority ordering are unit-tested and have not needed a single change since they were written — whatever the real location count and screen size turn out to be, that part is ready.
sourceContext: Ingram's mid-session message during the deck rebuild: 'Think about how the city map UI would look, V1 of the UI had character frames and map pin visuals which you need to create too.' Captured rather than built blind, because building it needs real location data this project doesn't have yet.
openSubQuestions: Does a city board belong to the Director only (a GM-side tactical view, like the cast board), or do players see it too (matching the downtime board's own 'everyone plans together, watching each other' shape)? day-ring.mjs's framing ('so I can plan around what others are doing') leans toward shared, but this hasn't been asked directly.

Real location data: how many named places does the campaign actually need at launch, who authors them, and do they get real coordinates against a real city map image or an abstracted schematic (V1's own MARKERS array mixed both address-like precision and pure fiction, e.g. 'the causeway')?

Is this the same screen as the downtime segment/offers zone (a location IS an offer, chosen by pin instead of by rotary selector), or a separate board that a downtime offer can link out to? The deck's current downtime selector (core/deck-layout.mjs's splitChecks/selectorState machinery) already solves 'choose one of several options with no coordinates' — a city board would only add something new if place actually matters to the choice.

Does `tools/city-map/`'s rendered raster output (a real Python image-generation pipeline, entirely separate code) ever become the actual background image here, or does this stay hand-illustrated/abstract indefinitely? The two tools have never been connected and nothing currently requires they ever are.
